title: The WebView command-boundary audit accepts an API route under the wrong HTTP method
observed_behavior: For every literal frontend call, the audit first looks up the exact method/path pair and then falls back to any contract with the same path. A POST call to a GET-only contract, or the inverse, therefore receives contract_found=true and inherits the other method's effect instead of producing undocumented-api-route.
expected_invariant: Frontend command auditing must require an exact HTTP method and normalized path match before reporting a contract, effect, confirmation classification, or high-risk disposition.
root_cause: routeContractsByPath deliberately discards the contract method and is used as a success fallback after the exact contractByPath lookup misses.
failure_scenario: A WebView edit changes apiGet('/api/example') to apiPost('/api/example') while only GET is declared. npm run webview:commands:check can remain green and report the GET effect for the POST, weakening the prework gate's route and high-risk evidence.
evidence: Current source SHA-256 b430086205d6de560d3a79a0176e0266cee67f151e00ddea92506152abf31917 builds both maps at lines 582-583 and applies exactLookup || pathOnlyLookup at line 638.
Read-only Node control reproduction with one GET /api/example contract and a requested POST returned requested=POST, declared=GET, contract_found=true, effect=read.
package.json makes this checker a direct member of webview:prework:check.
The Python report test independently compares method/path tuples, but that test is not part of the Node check command and does not repair the checker's own report or violation result.
existing_safeguards: The backend still rejects unsupported methods, and tests/webview/test_webview_command_boundary_audit.py separately checks generated method/path tuples when the Python suite is run.
safeguard_gap: The canonical Node prework checker can itself return success and emit a misleading effect before either safeguard runs; workflow and human callers treat its exit status as current command-boundary evidence.
tests_present: Current generated report matches the current backend tuple set.
Focused tests confirm split contract modules are scanned.
tests_missing: GET-only contract with a frontend POST usage.
POST-only contract with a frontend GET usage.
Assertion that path-only matches are violations and never supply effects.
recommended_remediation: Remove the path-only success fallback. Require contractByPath.get(`${method} ${normalized}`), report any same-path/different-method contracts only as diagnostic suggestions, and add method-mismatch fixtures to the Node and Python audit tests.
remediation_risk: Low: current routes already pass the independent tuple test, so the change should only expose future or latent method drift.
validation_rung: Focused WebView tooling tests plus webview:commands:check and webview:prework:check; representative real-media validation is not required.
prior_audit_relationship: New exact-current checker root cause. AUDIT-FIND-W12-006 concerns stale generated WebView baselines, not method-insensitive contract lookup.

title: Two high-risk packets are machine-complete while their required real-media release gates remain open
observed_behavior: Both version-2026.06.04.001 packets are status=complete and archived, but 0604-046 says representative real-media validation remains required before promotion and 0604-053 says the real-media worksheet/playbook was not run and must be rerun before release for pending-publish, sidecar, and final-placement changes.
expected_invariant: A high-risk packet selected as complete release evidence must either prove every explicitly required promotion gate or carry a machine-readable non-release-ready state that release selection enforces.
root_cause: Required validation outcomes exist only as free text. Packet validation treats any nonempty manual_validation list as completion evidence and does not reconcile outstanding-gate language with status; release-manifest/finalization selection uses status=complete.
failure_scenario: Release tooling selects these archived packets for the current 2026.06.04.001 release because they are complete, even though their own evidence states that required representative media validation has not happened. A release can therefore present machine-complete media-policy and pending-publish evidence without its named acceptance gate.
evidence: Current packet SHA-256 values are 7b8312bd2b080e638015d7c8912c926494edded9577930c285dca1e2c95b61d4 and 77b5e4ae0fdbd7cc1447f4296bfc20d095b8e965a866b606a8d29fce466d8e5c.
Direct packet_validation_errors plus archived-lifecycle validation returned zero errors for both packets.
Both packets have version_target=2026.06.04.001, matching ops/release/metadata/VERSION.

After generated summaries were read, current build_release_manifest.py lines 70-85 and finalize_release.py lines 49-55 were inspected: both select archived/unreleased packets solely by status=complete, with version matching applied by manifest construction.
existing_safeguards: The outstanding gates are candid in packet notes, focused unit/PowerShell/end-to-end checks passed, the no-touch register requires validation-first handling, and release actions remain operator initiated.
safeguard_gap: Free-text caveats are not a machine gate. The fields consumed by packet validation and release selection say complete, so automation cannot distinguish these packets from fully accepted high-risk evidence.
tests_present: Schema and archive-location validation for required fields/status/date.
Focused media, pending-publish, browser, and reliability tests recorded in the packets.
tests_missing: Validator rejection of complete high-risk packets with outstanding required gates.
Release-selection fixture proving incomplete representative-media evidence is excluded.
recommended_remediation: Add schema-backed validation gates with required/completed/not_applicable outcomes, or keep these packets in_progress until the required worksheets complete. Make manifest/finalization selection reject any complete high-risk packet with an open gate and migrate the two contradictory records.
remediation_risk: Medium: historical packet migration and release tooling must preserve legitimate negative-path validation records without interpreting every word such as failed or skipped as an open gate.
validation_rung: Change-control schema/validator/manifest/finalization fixture tests plus the representative real-media validation named by each packet before release; the audit itself did not run media.
prior_audit_relationship: New packet-evidence contradiction. Existing W10 release findings address workflow and package acceptance, while W11-024 addresses archival time-of-check drift rather than release-gate state.

title: MCP registration replacement deletes the prior client configuration before the new one succeeds
observed_behavior: With -Replace, each client registration is removed and only then re-added. If add fails, the script throws without restoring the previous registration; with -Clients Both, Codex may already be changed when Claude later fails.
expected_invariant: Replacing developer-client configuration should either leave every selected client on the requested new registration or preserve/restore the exact prior registration when any step fails.
root_cause: The script performs remove/add as irreversible sequential CLI calls and retains neither a restorable prior command/argument snapshot nor a multi-client rollback plan.
failure_scenario: A client accepts mcp remove but rejects mcp add because of a client-version, config-write, or argument error. The user's working prior mediapipeline-code registration is lost; a later Claude failure can also leave Both in a partially configured state while the overall command fails.
evidence: Current source SHA-256 85681af2e218c17851ec4b8d8eca4bf638d999fcb61c007c4e7fd043424e894e removes at lines 134-138/157-161 and throws on failed add at lines 140-143/163-166.
The apply sequence configures Codex before Claude at lines 227-234 and has no catch/finally rollback.
The focused MCP test exercises preview only; no fake-client replacement failure or partial Both-client fixture exists.
existing_safeguards: The environment is installed before registration changes, matching registrations are no-ops, differing registrations require explicit -Replace, and failed remove/add calls throw.
safeguard_gap: Preflight reduces dependency failures but cannot make client config writes infallible, and throwing after removal reports failure without recovering the configuration that existed on entry.
tests_present: Read-only preview smoke through the bundled PowerShell host.
tests_missing: Remove succeeds/add fails for each client.
Exact restoration of the prior command and argument vector.
recommended_remediation: Capture a structured, replayable prior registration for every selected client, preflight all add inputs, then replace transactionally. On any failure, restore every client already changed and report both the primary and rollback outcomes.
remediation_risk: Medium: Codex and Claude expose different registration formats/scopes, so restoration must be fixture-tested against supported CLI versions.
validation_rung: Focused temporary-config tests with stub Codex/Claude CLIs covering success, add failure, rollback failure, and Both-client partial failure; representative real-media validation is not required.
prior_audit_relationship: New developer-tool transactionality root; no existing finding mentions setup-code-context-mcp replacement or client-registration rollback.

title: Mistyped WebView check arguments can rewrite baselines, and invalid numeric thresholds silently erase candidates
observed_behavior: Six baseline tools determine mode with argv.includes and ignore every unknown token; no recognized --check means write mode. The godfile analyzer rejects unknown flags but converts arbitrary threshold text with Number() and accepts NaN, Infinity, zero, and negative values.
expected_invariant: Check/write generators must reject every unknown, missing, conflicting, non-finite, or out-of-range argument before reading or mutating a baseline.
root_cause: Most parsers test for known tokens without consuming and validating the full argv vector; the analyzer converts numeric arguments without Number.isFinite or range checks.
failure_scenario: An operator types --chek on a stale contract/route/DOM/split/lint report. The command defaults to write and refreshes the baseline instead of failing the intended check. Separately, --min-candidate-lines not-a-number exits 0 and reports zero split candidates, suppressing decomposition evidence.
evidence: The six mode parsers use argv.includes and default to write when --check is absent at the listed lines.
A read-only analyzer run with --json --min-candidate-lines not-a-number exited 0 over both default files and returned total_candidates=0; Number(NaN) controls both minimum-line and gap comparisons.
No target CLI test asserts unknown-option refusal, required option values, finite positive thresholds, or --check typo behavior.
package.json uses correct fixed options in canonical npm scripts, but these files are also documented/direct developer command surfaces.
existing_safeguards: Canonical npm scripts spell flags correctly, write modes still run their underlying analysis, generated diffs can be reviewed, and analyze-webview-godfiles rejects wholly unknown option names.
safeguard_gap: Direct commands can succeed in the opposite mode from operator intent, and a rewritten baseline can make the next correct check green. Git diff review is advisory and does not make the command fail.
tests_present: Functional current/stale report tests and lint-budget policy tests.
tests_missing: Unknown and misspelled flag rejection for every CLI.
recommended_remediation: Use one strict argument parser or a shared consume-all helper, require an explicit mode for direct baseline mutation, validate finite positive integer thresholds, and add temporary-output tests proving all argument errors exit nonzero without changing files.
remediation_risk: Low to medium: direct no-argument write workflows may need explicit --write updates in package scripts and documentation.
validation_rung: Focused Node/Python tooling tests in a temporary repository plus every webview:*:check command; representative real-media validation is not required.
prior_audit_relationship: New CLI root cause. W12-005/W12-006 record stale WebView artifacts, not the argument behavior that can accidentally rewrite or empty them.

title: GitHub label dry-run output cannot be replayed for descriptions containing spaces
observed_behavior: Apply mode correctly splats an argument array, but dry-run mode joins that array with spaces and emits it as a shell command without quoting. Every current label description contains spaces.
expected_invariant: A dry-run that prints the commands it would apply must preserve the exact argument vector so the preview is faithful and safely replayable.
root_cause: The preview serializes arguments with -join ' ' instead of a PowerShell/CLI-safe quoting routine or structured JSON.
failure_scenario: An operator copies the displayed gh label create command. PowerShell passes only the first word after --description as the option value and the remaining description words as unexpected positional arguments, so the documented bootstrap preview cannot be used to reproduce the apply action.
evidence: Current source SHA-256 4d0de3ba81c12d5d55fd9c53604912ccc319943cc7c300edcdb9148ab307920e applies with & gh @args at line 75 but previews with ($args -join ' ') at line 80.
A read-only preview exited 0 and emitted: gh label create audit --repo owner/repo --color 5319e7 --description Finding originated from audit, scanner, review, or AI-assisted analysis. --force.
All 23 current audit-label descriptions are multiword strings; none is quoted in preview output.
existing_safeguards: Actual -Apply execution uses array splatting and therefore preserves each description as one argument; -Apply also requires gh and a resolved repository.
safeguard_gap: The pre-mutation review surface is the malformed representation, so an operator cannot faithfully inspect/replay the exact command the script will invoke.
tests_missing: Round-trip preview of spaces, quotes, apostrophes, and shell metacharacters.
Assertion that preview and apply argument vectors are identical.
recommended_remediation: Emit a structured argument array or quote every argument with a tested PowerShell-safe serializer; ideally expose -WhatIf/ShouldProcess and test preview/apply equivalence with a stub gh executable.
remediation_risk: Low: apply semantics need not change.
validation_rung: PowerShell parser plus stub-gh dry-run/apply argument-vector tests; representative real-media validation is not required.
prior_audit_relationship: New dry-run fidelity defect; no existing finding covers bootstrap-github-audit-spine preview serialization.

title: Two unreleased packet sources again outpace their generated hashes
observed_behavior: The generated summary and PROJECT_INDEX entry for each packet agree with one another but fingerprint older packet bytes, not the exact current JSON reviewed in this slice.
expected_invariant: Generated navigation must bind every summarized packet to its exact current source hash, or explicitly withhold the summary until the packet settles.
root_cause: Both packet JSON files changed after their summaries and PROJECT_INDEX records were generated, under the same release-packet summary census gap already confirmed by AUDIT-FIND-W12-011.
failure_scenario: An agent follows the required summary-first workflow and receives outdated status, validation, or touched-path navigation for an active high-risk packet or the completed MCP tooling packet, then scopes review from evidence that no longer identifies the current bytes.
evidence: 0717-002 current SHA-256 is 3b5e82fcb35c15b703caa1d0c9f9d55aeb18fb59c85293137b8aa63b4b134c5d; its summary and PROJECT_INDEX record declare b743d861aeaa924d76752899a91b6f502c4e676823e09cc862097ae81f562a6f.

0720-010 current SHA-256 is 210046bc121f32b50504407e480d9b15b4070cfe8ae74fdf7df16ef1e382ab16; its summary and PROJECT_INDEX record declare b79aaddafb69c6b520e68991f70c904f0ff7d5791e56281cebdf7eec9f6090a5.
Fresh repository_audit_ledger build_rows over exactly 6,499 tracked paths marked project_index_present=true and project_index_hash_matches=false for both.
Both stale summaries were read before the complete current packet sources, so audit coverage did not inherit their stale content.
existing_safeguards: Summary frontmatter and PROJECT_INDEX retain a source SHA-256, allowing exact-current consumers to detect the mismatch; direct packet reads remain authoritative.
safeguard_gap: The navigation surfaces are still presented as current and require an external exact-hash comparison to discover the drift.
tests_present: Summary integrity and generator check tooling exists for covered summary classes.
tests_missing: Tracked release-packet summary census covering these two paths and every other tracked packet summary.
recommended_remediation: After packet writers settle, refresh both summaries and PROJECT_INDEX, then implement the full tracked release-packet summary census recommended by AUDIT-FIND-W12-011.
remediation_risk: Low for regeneration; coordinate with active packet writers to avoid immediate re-drift.
validation_rung: Exact source/summary hash pairing, full summary check, focused summary-integrity tests, and fresh 6,499-row audit inventory; representative real-media validation is not required for the metadata refresh.
prior_audit_relationship: Current exact-byte recurrence on the two packet sources after AUDIT-FIND-W12-010 recorded an earlier transient mismatch as resolved; AUDIT-FIND-W12-011 confirms the broader release-packet summary census gap.
